newsitem.title: USA: Tosco says extra heatoil coming from Bayway.
newsitem.headline: Tosco says extra heatoil coming from Bayway.

text.p: Tosco Corp's pledge to maximize distillate production to help build up low stocks in the Northeast will be fulfilled by its Bayway refinery in Linden, New Jersey, a Tosco executive told Reuters.
He also noted Tosco's newly-acquired and currently-idle Trainer, Pennsylvania refinery will not produce any distillates this winter.
"Bayway has gone into 'max" heating oil production mode," the Tosco executive said. "Trainer will not produce any heating oil this winter," he said.

The executive said the Tosco output boost, announced Friday by U.S. Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary in Washington after her meeting with oil executives to discuss low stocks, is part of an ongoing push to raise output at the refinery.
He noted Bayway's distillate output, now at around 90,000 to 100,000 barrels per day, has nearly doubled since Tosco bought the plant from Exxon Corp in 1993.
He also said Tosco's own distillate stocks are not low.
"Our inventory levels right now are comparable to last year," the executive said.

But heating oil stocks on the whole East Coast, the largest heating oil market in the world, stood 43 percent below year-ago levels at the end of last week, or at about 24.3 million barrels, according to data from the American Petroleum Institute.

In response to a question, the Tosco executive said that the idling of the Trainer refinery near Philadelphia could be one of the reasons stocks are lower than last year since active refineries are typically adjacent to large tank farms.

But industry sources have cited a host of other factors keeping stocks low, including corporate programs aimed at cutting stocks to boost working capital, strong export demand from Europe and a marketplace that is providing no economic incentive for refiners to build their inventories.

He also noted that when Tosco brings the Trainer refinery back to life next summer, it will have throughput capacity of about 150,000 barrels per day (bpd), and will be able to produce some 50,000 to 60,000 bpd of distillates.
He noted however that distillates include motor diesel and jet fuel as well as heating oil, with relative output of each fuel often linked to market opportunities.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
